name: asana
label: Asana
note: Asana's REST API with a personal access token. Call it as /gw/asana/users/me; the /api/1.0 prefix is already in the address.

name: cloudflare
label: Cloudflare
note: Cloudflare's v4 API with an API token, sent as a bearer token. The older Global API Key is a different pair of headers and is not what we send.

name: github
label: GitHub
note: The GitHub REST API with a token you already hold. Nothing here performs GitHub's OAuth or App-installation flows, so store a token rather than expecting one to be minted.

name: linear
label: Linear
note: Linear's GraphQL API at /gw/linear/graphql. Linear reads a personal API key as the bare Authorization value with no Bearer word, which is what we send; an OAuth token is the other shape and would need an upstream of its own.

name: gitlab
label: GitLab
note: GitLab.com's REST API with a personal, project or group access token sent as a bearer token; a self-managed GitLab lives at the customer's own domain and needs an address of its own rather than this entry.

name: bitbucket
label: Bitbucket Cloud
note: Bitbucket Cloud's REST API with an Atlassian API token or an access token as a bearer token; the older app-password style needs the account email as a basic-auth username and is not what we send.

name: vercel
label: Vercel
note: Vercel's REST API with an access token. A token scoped to a team needs the teamId query parameter on most paths, which the caller supplies; nothing here adds it.

name: netlify
label: Netlify
note: Netlify's API with a personal access token. File uploads to a deploy use a different content type but the same address and token.

name: render
label: Render
note: Render's REST API with an API key created in the dashboard; Render has no separate read-only key, so whatever is stored here can also change services.

name: fly
label: Fly.io
note: Fly's Machines API with a Fly access token. Fly's older GraphQL API at api.fly.io is a different address and is not covered by this entry.

name: digitalocean
label: DigitalOcean
note: DigitalOcean's v2 API with a personal access token; Spaces uses S3-style request signing instead and cannot be reached through this.

name: linode
label: Linode
note: The Linode (Akamai Cloud) v4 API with a personal access token. Akamai's other product APIs use EdgeGrid signing and are not this address.

name: hetzner
label: Hetzner Cloud
note: Hetzner Cloud's API with a project API token. Hetzner's DNS and Robot APIs read different headers and are not covered here.

name: circleci
label: CircleCI
note: CircleCI's v2 API with a personal API token sent as a bearer token, which CircleCI documents as the recommended of its three placements; the Circle-Token header is the same credential in a header we do not set.

name: buildkite
label: Buildkite
note: Buildkite's REST API with an API access token. Buildkite's GraphQL API is a separate address and its agent token is a different credential entirely.

name: codecov
label: Codecov
note: Codecov's v2 API with an API token. The upload token used by CI to post coverage is a different credential and goes to a different endpoint.

name: sonarcloud
label: SonarQube Cloud
note: SonarQube Cloud's web API with a user token as a bearer token; the US instance at sonarqube.us and any self-managed SonarQube Server are separate addresses.

name: semgrep
label: Semgrep
note: Semgrep AppSec Platform's API with an API token. Running the semgrep scanner itself is a local process and never touches this address.

name: npm
label: npm registry
note: The public npm registry with an access token. Package metadata and tarballs are readable without any token, so only writes and private packages need this stored.

name: jsr
label: JSR
note: The JSR registry's management API with a personal access token; the public package-metadata endpoints need no token at all.

name: cratesio
label: crates.io
note: The crates.io registry API, which reads the API token as the bare Authorization value with no scheme word, exactly as Cargo sends it.

name: rubygems
label: RubyGems.org
note: RubyGems.org's API, which reads the API key as the bare Authorization value; a key scoped by RubyGems' permission list can be refused per endpoint even though the address is right.

name: quay
label: Quay.io
note: Quay.io's management API with an OAuth 2 access token generated in the UI; pulling and pushing images uses the registry protocol on the same host and is not this API.

name: clickup
label: ClickUp
note: ClickUp's API, which reads a personal token as the bare Authorization value with no Bearer word; an OAuth access token is the other shape and would need an upstream of its own.

name: monday
label: monday.com
note: monday.com's GraphQL API at /gw/monday/v2, which reads the API token as the bare Authorization value with no Bearer word; every real call is a POST of a GraphQL document.

name: plane
label: Plane
note: Plane Cloud's API with a workspace API key in X-API-Key; a self-hosted Plane lives at the customer's own domain and needs an address of its own.

name: postman
label: Postman
note: The Postman API with an API key in X-API-Key. Postman's EU data residency uses a different host and is not this entry.

name: raygun
label: Raygun
note: Raygun's API with a personal access token; the API key an application uses to send crash reports is a different credential.

name: honeybadger
label: Honeybadger
note: Honeybadger's data API, which takes the personal auth token as the HTTP basic username with no password; the project API key used to report errors is a different credential.

name: airbrake
label: Airbrake
note: Airbrake's v4 API with a user key; the project key that an SDK uses to report errors is a different credential and a different endpoint.

name: socketdev
label: Socket
note: Socket's API, which takes the API token as the HTTP basic username with an empty password, the form its own documentation gives.

name: fossa
label: FOSSA
note: FOSSA's API with an API token; a push-only token is refused on most read paths even though the address is correct.

name: terraform
label: HCP Terraform
note: HCP Terraform's API with a user, team or organization token; a Terraform Enterprise install lives at the customer's own domain and needs an address of its own.

name: doppler
label: Doppler
note: Doppler's API with a personal, service or service-account token. Everything it returns is secret material, so a receipt for this traffic is a record of secrets moving.

name: split
label: Split
note: Split's admin API with an admin API key; the SDK keys used by an application are different credentials and do not work here.

name: growthbook
label: GrowthBook
note: GrowthBook Cloud's REST API with a secret API key; a self-hosted GrowthBook lives at the customer's own domain and needs an address of its own.

name: mergify
label: Mergify
note: Mergify's API with an application API key, which is scoped to one organization or repository when it is created.

name: buddy
label: Buddy
note: Buddy's cloud API with a personal access token; a Buddy On-Premises install lives at the customer's own domain and needs an address of its own.

name: appveyor
label: AppVeyor
note: AppVeyor's REST API with an account API token; an AppVeyor Server install is a different host.

name: bitrise
label: Bitrise
note: Bitrise's API, which reads a personal access token as the bare Authorization value with no scheme word.

name: runpod
label: RunPod
note: RunPod's REST API with an API key; a serverless endpoint's own invoke URL is a different host and would need an upstream of its own.

name: koyeb
label: Koyeb
note: Koyeb's control-plane API with a personal or organization API token.

name: northflank
label: Northflank
note: Northflank's API with an API token, whose scope is fixed when the token is made; a self-hosted Northflank is a different address.

name: denodeploy
label: Deno Deploy
note: Deno Deploy's REST API with an access token; the deployed applications themselves are on separate hosts and are not reached through this.

name: pipedream
label: Pipedream
note: Pipedream's REST API with a user API key; a workflow's own HTTP trigger is a separate address and carries no key at all.

name: val
label: Val Town
note: Val Town's REST API with an API token; the HTTP vals a customer publishes run on their own subdomains and are not reached through this.

name: ngrok
label: ngrok
note: ngrok's management API with an API key; the agent authtoken that opens a tunnel is a different credential. Most paths also want an Ngrok-Version header, which the caller supplies.

name: tailscale
label: Tailscale
note: Tailscale's API, which takes the access token as the HTTP basic username with no password; an OAuth client must first exchange itself for a token and that flow is not performed here.

name: keycdn
label: KeyCDN
note: KeyCDN's API, which takes the API key as the HTTP basic username with no password, the form its own documentation gives.

name: imgix
label: imgix
note: imgix's management API with an API key; the image-rendering domains are separate hosts and their URLs are signed with a different secret.

name: ionos
label: IONOS Cloud
note: IONOS Cloud's v6 API with a token from the token manager; the older username-and-password basic form is a different credential and is not what we send.

name: latitudesh
label: Latitude.sh
note: Latitude.sh's API with an API key; some paths also want an API-Version header, which the caller supplies.

name: hostinger
label: Hostinger
note: Hostinger's developer API with an API token; it covers VPS, domains and DNS only, not shared hosting or the control panel.

name: vultr
label: Vultr
note: Vultr's v2 API with an API key; the key is refused unless the calling address is on the account's API access allowlist, so a correct entry can still be rejected from a new egress address.

name: youtrack
label: YouTrack
template_hint: the name in your YouTrack address, before .youtrack.cloud
note: YouTrack Cloud's REST API with a permanent token; a self-managed YouTrack or an older youtrack.jetbrains.com address is a different host, and this entry was read off JetBrains' own page rather than probed, because the address is not known until the customer names their instance.

name: gitea
label: Gitea
note: Gitea reads an access token as the literal word token, a space, then the key. A Bearer prefix is accepted only for OAuth2 tokens, so sending one for a personal access token fails with a JWT parse error rather than a credential error.

name: codeberg
label: Codeberg
note: Codeberg runs Forgejo, a Gitea fork, and takes the same token word before the key. Its 401 body quotes the rejected token back verbatim, so a reply from this upstream can contain the customer's own key — worth knowing before turning stored content on for it.

name: sourcegraph
label: Sourcegraph
note: Sourcegraph reads the word token before the access token. A bare token gets Invalid Authorization header, which reads like a bad key and is not.

name: snyk
label: Snyk
note: Snyk's API tokens are sent as the word token before the key.
